title: smart-routing-fallback-debug-notes-jasmin
content:
Incident breadcrumbs / debug scratchpad - smart routing fallback + regional failover

Summary:
- Short: on 2025-11-02 14:12 UTC we saw elevated 5xxs from eu-west-1 model endpoints; smart-routing should have failed over to eu-central-1 but requests continued to be routed to the degraded capacity for ~7m. During that window customer A experienced errors and latency spikes.
- Goal: capture commands tried, error snippets, timeline, hypotheses, and next actions for a postmortem draft.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2025-11-02 14:08 - first uptick in 5xx from eu-west-1 (alerts: error-rate > 3% for 2m).
- 2025-11-02 14:10 - alert escalated to oncall; we saw lower available capacity (pods OOM / preempted?).
- 2025-11-02 14:12 - oncall disabled autoscaler for eu-west-1 to stop churn (temporary).
- 2025-11-02 14:13 - smart-routing policy should trigger regional-failover after 30s of elevated errors; routing logs show continued route decisions to eu-west-1 until 14:19.
- 2025-11-02 14:20 - manual routing override to eu-central-1 initiated.
- 2025-11-02 14:25 - traffic back to normal.

Commands run / logs collected (snips):
- kubectl (checked pods & recent restarts):
  kubectl -n infra get pods -l region=eu-west-1 -o wide
  # output: 6/10 running, 4 CrashLoopBackOff (OOMKilled)

- pod logs (example):
  kubectl -n infra logs redwood-serving-xyz-7f6b -c inference \n    --since=30m | sed -n '1,120p'
  # snippets:
  # 2025-11-02T14:09:34Z ERROR KvCache: failed to allocate 256MB for kv-cache: OOMKilled
  # 2025-11-02T14:09:34Z WARN RequestHandler: slow path fallback - falling back to single-threaded kernel
  # 2025-11-02T14:11:58Z ERROR ModelLoader: reloading model instance failed: out of memory

- routing service (trace):
  curl -s "https://routing-redwood-int/api/v1/route?key=svc-test&region_preference=eu" | jq .
  # trace timeline: decision -> eu-west-1 at 14:12:01 (score=0.82), fail_count=1
  # subsequent decisions at 14:13..14:18 still pick eu-west-1, scores degrade but still above threshold until manual override

- routing logs (grep):
  grep "route_decision" /var/log/routing/*.log | sed -n '1,200p'
  # example line:
  # 2025-11-02T14:13:10Z route_decision svc-test -> eu-west-1 (score=0.62) [metrics: p95=420ms, errors=4.5%]

- policy config (current):
  # smart-routing-policy.yaml (snippet)
  fallback_policies:
    - name: regional-failover
      trigger: "error_rate > 3% for 30s"
      fallback_to: nearest_region
      cooldown: 300s
      max_fallbacks: 2

Observations / mismatches:
- Trigger condition matched earlier (errors > 3%), but the router continued to route to same region. Routing logs show score trending down but not crossing the internal threshold computed by the scoring function.
- Possible race between autoscaler (which was scaling down due to OOM churn) and the router's health probes. When autoscaler toggled instance states, the health metric feed to router may have been delayed/partial.
- There is a known issue where when the capacity reports change rapidly, the scoring function applies stabilization window (30s) and uses stale metrics for some traffic shards (see TODO link to bug). This could delay failover.

Error snippets collected:
- 502 / 503 seen by customers: "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers"
- Pod logs: "OOMKilled", "failed to allocate"
- Router: "policy eval: regional-failover - not triggered (score=0.62 < threshold=0.6)" (note: logs show threshold=0.6, but route still kept choosing eu-west-1 - need to reconcile)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Metric propagation delay: health/telemetry updates from autoscaler and infra didn't reach the routing service quickly enough (or were aggregated per-minute) causing router to see outdated capacity and not trigger failover.
2) Scoring bug: the score normalization or threshold comparison has an off-by-one or floating precision issue. Some logs say score 0.62 and threshold 0.6 but router kept routing — maybe another tie-breaker (prefer local region) overrides policy.
3) Fallback policy precedence: the canary/rollback policy or per-customer override took precedence and prevented automatic regional failover for some customers. Need to check route affinity configs.
4) Autoscaler interactions: scaling events created transient healthy=false signals that confused the router into thinking instances would recover quickly, so it waited.

Quick experiments to reproduce locally / next debug steps:
- Re-run router scoring locally with synthetic telemetry spike to see decision boundary. (script: tools/scoring/simulate_spike.py)
- Add extra logging around policy-eval path to capture all inputs (latency, error_rate, capacity, pref_score).
- Temporarily reduce trigger window to 10s in staging to validate faster failover (note: risk of flapping).
- Check whether shard affinity config has per-customer overrides: curl the routing-control API for svc-test
  curl -s "https://routing-control/api/v1/overrides?service=svc-test"

Notes from quick experiments (14:50-15:10):
- Running simulation with identical metrics produced score ~0.59 when we include a 5% pref bias for local region -> this explains why router preferred eu-west-1 even when errors were slightly high.
- Found code path in scoring where local_region_bias was added after threshold comparison, effectively preventing fallback until bias removed. See PR TODO.

Immediate mitigation taken:
- Manual override at 14:20 to route svc-test -> eu-central-1 for 10m (ops runbook).
- Disable autoscaler toggling on eu-west-1 (so capacity not churned) and restart problematic pods with larger heap.

Postmortem action items (draft):
- Short term (P0/P1):
  - Remove local_region_bias from scoring function or move it into the score calculation before threshold check. (owner: Ethan)
  - Improve telemetry propagation: ensure health metrics propagate within 10s for routing decisions. (owner: Olivia)
  - Add observability: include pre/post policy-eval snapshot in routing logs for 7d retention. (owner: Jasmin)
- Medium term:
  - Run chaos tests to simulate rapid capacity loss and validate failover.
  - Revisit default fallback window and cooldown to avoid flapping while ensuring quick recovery.
  - Add automated rollback playbook to detect mis-configured local-region bias.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Why did policy eval log say score=0.62 and threshold=0.6 but still choose eu-west-1? Need deeper trace of decision ordering.
- Confirm whether per-customer routing affinity rule existed for this tenant (svc-test). If yes, was it applied?
- Verify the telemetry pipeline SLA (how fresh are metrics ingested by routing service?).

References / links:
- JIRA-2217 (incident ticket)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/489 (WIP local-bias fix)
- routing playbook: CONFLUENCE-serve-routing-playbook

Scratchpad / misc commands to re-run later:
- kubectl -n infra describe hpa redwood-serving-eu-west-1
- kubectl -n infra logs -l app=routing --since=1h | grep regional-failover
- curl -s "https://routing-control/api/v1/configs/global" | jq .fallback_policies

Short note to self: prioritize reproducible unit test for scoring + add an integration smoke test that flips one region to 0 capacity and verifies alt region gets >95% of traffic within 60s.

-- Jasmin
